\section[validus, valida, validum]{validus, valida, validum — strong}

\label{lesson:LA-C152-validus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for ugly, then the Latin for beautiful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: validus, valida, validum}
\textbf{validus, valida, validum} — \textquotedblleft{}strong\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{validus} is built on \emph{valeō}, \textquotedblleft{}to be strong\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with \emph{-idus}, the ending of state adjectives. \emph{valeō} is usually traced to Proto-Indo-European \emph{*h2welh1-}, \textquotedblleft{}to be strong, to rule\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{validus}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{validus}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{validus}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for ugly, then the Latin for beautiful, then say \emph{validus} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does validus, valida, validum mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Strong\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[īnfirmus, īnfirma, īnfirmum]{īnfirmus, īnfirma, īnfirmum — weak}

\label{lesson:LA-C152-infirmus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for beautiful, then the Latin for strong.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: īnfirmus, īnfirma, īnfirmum}
\textbf{īnfirmus, īnfirma, īnfirmum} — \textquotedblleft{}weak\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{īnfirmus} is \emph{in-}, \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{firmus}, \textquotedblleft{}firm, strong\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short). \emph{firmus} is usually traced to Proto-Indo-European \emph{*dher-}, \textquotedblleft{}to hold, to support\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[sōlus, sōla, sōlum]{sōlus, sōla, sōlum — alone, only}

\label{lesson:LA-C152-solus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for strong, then the Latin for weak.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: sōlus, sōla, sōlum}
\textbf{sōlus, sōla, sōlum} — \textquotedblleft{}alone, only\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{sōlus} has no sure origin. It may belong with the reflexive \emph{sē}, \textquotedblleft{}oneself\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1 records Proto-Indo-European \emph{*swe}, \textquotedblleft{}self, alone\textquotedblright{}); Lewis \& Short link it with \emph{sollus}, \textquotedblleft{}whole\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}
